config.theme: Go/no-go for the Aurora mobile app launch
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Go/no-go for the Aurora mobile app launch

personas.name: Helen
personas.role: Director of digital services, chairs the review
personas.goals: A launch the agency won't have to apologize for
personas.hidden_agenda: The board chair rides the 14 bus and will try the app on day one

personas.name: Sipho
personas.hidden_agenda: Wants one more regression pass he hasn't asked for yet

personas.name: Marta
personas.goals: Riders with disabilities can use it from day one
personas.hidden_agenda: Ran some test sessions informally and counts them

personas.name: Jonah
personas.hidden_agenda: The real-time feed vendor has been flaky and he's nervous

agenda.title: Accessibility
agenda.goal: Confirm the audit status and remaining issues

facts.statement: Trip plans matching actual arrivals within 2 minutes = 96%

beats.summary: Stability, bugs and accuracy; Jonah undercounts the bugs and Sipho corrects him
Audit status; Marta's session count is higher than the record and stays that way
Support, the real-time feed and the press release date

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: Thank you all for coming. We'll go through quality, accessibility and operations, and then make the call. Sipho, would you start with stability?

turns.speaker: Sipho
turns.text: Crash-free users in the beta are at ninety-nine point six percent.

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: Against a target of ninety-nine point five.

turns.speaker: Sipho
turns.text: Yes. Just above. For completeness, the beta is small, so I'd treat that as encouraging rather than proven.

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: How many riders are in the beta now?

turns.speaker: Jonah
turns.text: Twenty-eight hundred. Mostly on the busier routes.

turns.speaker: Marta
turns.text: Which skews toward commuters. We have fewer older riders than I'd like.

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: That's worth noting. What about bugs?

turns.speaker: Jonah
turns.text: So, we're down to two severity-two bugs, which I'm pleased about.

turns.speaker: Sipho
turns.text: I have five open in the tracker. Two were fixed this week, which might be what you're thinking of.

turns.speaker: Jonah
turns.text: Ah, yes. Five open, two fixed. You're right.

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: What are the five?

turns.speaker: Sipho
turns.text: Three are display issues on older Android phones. One is a timetable that doesn't refresh after midnight. One is the fare calculator rounding.

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: The fare calculator rounding sounds like the kind of thing that ends up in the newspaper.

turns.speaker: Jonah
turns.text: It's a few cents in edge cases, but I agree it's visible.

turns.speaker: Sipho
turns.text: For completeness, the midnight timetable one worries me more. Night riders depend on it.

turns.speaker: Jonah
turns.text: The midnight refresh is a small fix. I'll have someone on it tomorrow and aim to close it this week.

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: And accuracy? Are trip plans matching reality?

turns.speaker: Jonah
turns.text: Ninety-six percent of trip plans match actual arrivals within two minutes.

turns.speaker: Marta
turns.text: Riders in the interviews said it felt more accurate than the old app.

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: That's encouraging. And the store rating in beta?

turns.speaker: Sipho
turns.text: Four point four, from about three hundred reviews.

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: All right. Quality looks reasonable, with the midnight timetable and the fare rounding as the two to watch.

turns.speaker: Jonah
turns.text: It snowed so much on the north side this morning that the 22 didn't run at all.

turns.speaker: Sipho
turns.text: My street still hasn't been plowed. I walked to the train in hiking boots.

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: Let's move on. Marta, accessibility?

turns.speaker: Marta
turns.text: We've closed most of the audit. Four WCAG issues are still open.

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: Are any of them blockers?

turns.speaker: Marta
turns.text: One is. The route map can't be explored with a screen reader. The other three are contrast and labels.

turns.speaker: Jonah
turns.text: The route map is the hardest one. It's a custom component.

turns.speaker: Marta
turns.text: We've run twelve screen-reader test sessions so far, and the map came up in almost every one.

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: Then the map matters. What would it take to fix it?

turns.speaker: Jonah
turns.text: A text alternative for the map, listing the stops in order, is about a week of work.

turns.speaker: Marta
turns.text: That would actually be better for a lot of people, not just screen-reader users.

turns.speaker: Sipho
turns.text: I can put that alternative through a regression pass once it's ready.

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: Thank you, Sipho. Jonah, would a week fit before March third?

turns.speaker: Jonah
turns.text: It would be tight, but yes, if we start Monday.

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: Then the text alternative for the route map is a launch requirement.

turns.speaker: Marta
turns.text: I'll sit with the developers on Monday and go through what the text version needs to say.

turns.speaker: Jonah
turns.text: Could we ship the contrast fixes in the first update instead of at launch?

turns.speaker: Marta
turns.text: I'd prefer launch, but the contrast issues are minor. I can live with the first update.

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: Let's look at how the week goes before we decide on the contrast fixes.

turns.speaker: Jonah
turns.text: Fair.

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: Operations. Who's ready on the support side?

turns.speaker: Marta
turns.text: Customer service has trained twenty-two people on the new app.

turns.speaker: Sipho
turns.text: Is that enough for launch week?

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: It's more than we had for the last app. I think it's enough.

turns.speaker: Jonah
turns.text: The thing that worries me is the real-time feed. Uptime was ninety-nine point one percent over the last month.

turns.speaker: Sipho
turns.text: For completeness, that's about six or seven hours of the feed being down in a month.

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: What happens in the app when the feed is down?

turns.speaker: Jonah
turns.text: It falls back to the timetable, with a little banner. Riders can still plan trips.

turns.speaker: Marta
turns.text: The banner needs to be read out by a screen reader too. I'll check that it is.

turns.speaker: Jonah
turns.text: Sorry, my connection dropped for a second. What did I miss?

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: Only Marta checking the banner. Nothing else.

turns.speaker: Jonah
turns.text: Got it, thanks.

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: And the press release goes out on the twenty-fifth, I believe.

turns.speaker: Jonah
turns.text: I'll ask the vendor for their maintenance calendar, so nothing's planned for launch week.

turns.speaker: Sipho
turns.text: It might be worth having someone from engineering on call that first weekend.

turns.speaker: Marta
turns.text: Communications sent the schedule this morning. The press release is the twenty-seventh, not the twenty-fifth.

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: The twenty-seventh. Thank you, Marta.

turns.speaker: Sipho
turns.text: Good catch.

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: So. Are we ready to go on March third?

turns.speaker: Sipho
turns.text: With the midnight timetable fixed and the route map alternative in, I'm comfortable.

turns.speaker: Marta
turns.text: Same conditions for me. The map has to be in.

turns.speaker: Jonah
turns.text: Agreed. We can do both.

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: Then it's a go for March third, on those two conditions.

turns.speaker: Sipho
turns.text: For completeness, I'd like one more full regression pass the week before. Is that possible?

turns.speaker: Jonah
turns.text: Yes. We'll freeze the code on the twenty-fourth to make room for it.

turns.speaker: Sipho
turns.text: Then I'll run the full regression pass starting on the twenty-fifth.

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: Who will tell the board chair? He'll be on the 14 bus on day one.

turns.speaker: Jonah
turns.text: Has anyone checked how the app behaves on the old tablets in the bus shelters?

turns.speaker: Helen
turns.text: Thank you, everyone. A careful review. We'll meet again the week before launch.
